{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -J PCC_optimzer
#   -q elektro
#   -n 1
#   -R "rusage[mem=2GB]"
#   -M 10GB
#   -W 20:00
#   -u alherm@dtu.dk
#   -B
#   -N
#   -o output_alex_run1.out
#   -e error_alex_run1.err
#   -R "span[hosts=1]"

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --time=20h \
  --queue=elektro \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate LSF stdout/stderr files
exec >output_alex_run1.out 2>error_alex_run1.err

# NOTE: LSF memory requests (-R rusage[mem=2GB] and -M 10GB) have no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: LSF email notifications (-u/-B/-N) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive start/end emails.

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J PCC_optimzer) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: LSF placement constraint (-R span[hosts=1]) has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: if multiple tasks were used, they might span hosts; here -n 1 so it is effectively moot.

module load cvx
module load mosek/9.2
##module load gurobi/8.1.1

matlab -nodisplay -r RUN_PCC_optim -logfile PCC_optim_logfile_output
'
"
}
